skill.name: video-shots
skill.description: Analyzes videos shot by shot with ffmpeg measurements, structured annotations, quality checks, contact sheets, and interactive offline reports.
skill.summary: Create measured, reviewable shot breakdowns from local video files.
skill.author: eternityspring

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by JavaScript syntax, readable documentation, test fixtures, and deliberate ffmpeg execution through argument arrays. Four report-rendering paths are confirmed XSS risks because unescaped identifiers or frame paths can reach innerHTML in generated offline reports. Static review was capped at 400/512 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 112 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Generated reports insert some shot identifiers and frame-directory values into innerHTML without attribute escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Build these elements with DOM APIs and set textContent, dataset, and src properties directly. Otherwise, apply context-specific attribute escaping before insertion.

remediation.issue: The render command can process a shots document even when identifiers fail validation.
remediation.suggestion: Reject invalid shot identifiers before rendering and constrain frame paths to expected local directories. Add tests using quotes and HTML event attributes.

medium_findings.title: innerHTML assignment (XSS risk)
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The timeline markup places each document-supplied shot id into an HTML attribute without escaping. Rendering a crafted shots document can therefore create executable markup in the offline report.

medium_findings.title: innerHTML assignment (XSS risk)
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: Card markup interpolates unescaped shot ids and frame paths into attributes before assigning innerHTML. A crafted shots document or frame-directory argument can inject executable markup.

medium_findings.title: innerHTML assignment (XSS risk)
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The analysis summary inserts longest.id and shortest.id through replacement strings without escaping before assigning innerHTML. Crafted shot identifiers can break into markup.

medium_findings.title: innerHTML assignment (XSS risk)
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: Cast-card image markup is built with the frame directory in an unescaped src attribute before assigning innerHTML. A crafted frame-directory value can inject markup when frames exist.

content.value_statement: Manual shot breakdowns are slow and timing estimates are unreliable. This skill measures cuts and motion, then produces structured reviews and interactive reports.
actual_capabilities: Detects scene cuts and video metadata with ffmpeg and ffprobe.
Measures per-shot duration and frame-change motion values.
Extracts opening and closing keyframes for each shot.
Builds contact sheets for comparing composition and camera movement.
Validates annotations through 15 deterministic quality gates.
Renders Markdown summaries and interactive offline HTML reports.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or later, ffmpeg, and ffprobe on the local system.
Does not transcribe speech or identify people automatically.
Scene detection can miss dissolves or split flashes and handheld movement.
Camera-motion measurements cannot separate camera movement from subject movement.

use_cases.title: Review Editing Rhythm
use_cases.description: Measure shot lengths, cut frequency, categories, and rhythm roles across a finished edit.

use_cases.title: Study Cinematography
use_cases.description: Compare shot sizes, camera movement, subjects, and opening or closing frames.

use_cases.title: Inventory Campaign Footage
use_cases.description: Find product shots, title cards, dialogue, and reusable visual patterns in delivered videos.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Breakdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this video shot by shot. Use default detection settings and create the shot data, keyframes, contact sheets, and report.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first analysis with standard settings.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Editing Rhythm
prompt_templates.prompt: Break down this video for editing rhythm. Include shot durations, cut frequency, categories, rhythm roles, and the longest and shortest shots.
prompt_templates.scenario: A pacing review for an editor.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Detection Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this video, review the contact sheets for missed or extra cuts, apply recut corrections, and rerun every quality gate.
prompt_templates.scenario: A careful breakdown with corrected scene boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Comparative Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these videos separately, validate each result, then compare shot size, camera movement, category, and rhythm distributions in a concise report.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced comparison across several finished videos.

output_examples.input: Analyze a 60-second product advertisement for pacing and camera movement.
output: A measured shot table with time ranges, durations, shot sizes, categories, movement, and descriptions.
Opening and closing keyframes plus contact sheets for visual comparison.
An offline report with filters, distributions, playback navigation, and quality-gate results.

output_examples.input: Review a short film and identify missed dissolves before reporting.
output_examples.output: A corrected shot breakdown with declared manual cuts, recalculated timing, refreshed keyframes, and a validation summary.

best_practices: Review contact sheets before opening individual frames.
Record every manual split or merge through the recut command.
Run validation with motion data and keyframes before rendering the final report.
anti_patterns: Do not estimate shot boundaries or durations from visual inspection.
Do not edit measured timing, motion, or metadata fields by hand.
Do not treat skipped quality gates as successful checks.

faq.question: What software does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Node.js 18 or later, ffmpeg, and ffprobe. It has no npm package dependencies.

faq.question: Does it transcribe dialogue?
faq.answer: No. It can record visible subtitles, but it does not include speech recognition.

faq.question: Can it identify actors automatically?
faq.answer: No. Cast identifiers and person grouping require manual review.

faq.question: How are shot boundaries detected?
faq.answer: ffmpeg scene scores provide initial cuts. The recut workflow records reviewed splits and merges.

faq.question: Can it analyze camera movement reliably?
faq.answer: It compares keyframes with measured frame changes. Subject motion can still resemble camera motion.

faq.question: Can the report work without internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The generated HTML report is self-contained, but video and keyframe files remain local.
